quarterly_data.signal: Venglustat NDA in type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) accepted for FDA priority review (release of May 28, 2026). If approved it would be the first treatment available in the US for the progressive neurological manifestations of GD3. The NDA rests on the LEAP2MONO phase 3 study (43 patients randomized 1:1 to oral venglustat or intravenous enzyme replacement therapy), in which venglustat met both primary endpoints (SARA modified total score and RBANS total scale index score at week 52) and three out of four key secondary endpoints, and was well tolerated with no new safety signals; the most common adverse events were headache (14.3% vs 18.2% on ERT), nausea (14.3% vs 4.5%), spleen enlargement (14.3% vs 0) and diarrhea (14.3% vs 0). Venglustat previously earned FDA breakthrough therapy and fast-track designations in GD3 and orphan designation in the US, EU and Japan; it is also under regulatory review in the EU, and Sanofi will pursue additional global filings in GD3 in 2026.
